key_insight: The classical 2-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm stabilizes in linear time, with a proven upper bound of 5(n−1) rounds, matching the known Ω(n) lower bound up to a constant factor.
engineering_relevance: This gives a tighter worst-case runtime guarantee for graph isomorphism and related symmetry-detection pipelines that use Weisfeiler-Leman refinement.
method: Prove a linear upper bound on stabilization rounds for the classical 2-WL algorithm.
Extend the argument to k-WL for every k ≥ 3, yielding improved bounds of O(n^{k-1}/(k-2)! + n^{k-2}).
Generalize the proof to a broader class of tuple-coloring sequences, where the bounds are essentially tight.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a new theoretical upper bound of 5(n−1), improving the previous O(n log n) bound and aligning with the known Ω(n) lower bound.
watch_item: These are worst-case iteration bounds; practical runtime can still depend heavily on graph size, structure, and implementation details.
paper_title: The Classical Weisfeiler-Leman Algorithm Stabilizes in $O(n)$ Rounds
